plain_description.what: On 3,222 MASSIVE intent queries whose slot words were swapped (e.g. a different city name), it asks what predicts a query jumping to a different k-means cell. Candidates are how close the original sat to a cell boundary and how much of the text was swapped, with a descriptive look at the embedder.
plain_description.why: An earlier test found cells unstable under slot swaps. This test tries to explain why, and whether flagging near-boundary queries could help.
plain_description.information: If boundary closeness predicts flips, low-confidence queries could be flagged. If swap size predicts flips, the instability is driven by surface wording. Result: done. Both predict flips. Near-boundary queries flipped 55% of the time vs 8% for the safest fifth, and larger swaps flipped more even at fixed boundary distance. These are associations, not causes (swap share is mixed up with text length). Not shown: that boundary-gating fixes the problem. The embedder look is descriptive only, one seed, not a ranking.
